style: Say in a clear, informative way, like a nature documentary narrator
lines: Here is the Turbo Gecko ad. Tap Play, then Pause wherever something looks too good.
Drag a trick card onto the picture. Or tap the picture, then tap a card.
Six claims. Now let us test them. Tap The lab.
Pick a test. The real toy is on the table.
Now mark the claim: holds up, stretched, or not in the box.
The evidence is in. Tap The verdict.
Pick the ad message. Then choose two claim cards to support it.
Tap Cards to review your supporting claims, or tap Ratings to review your judgment.
Back it up. Add a piece of evidence to your rating.
Case closed. Ask these four questions about the next ad you see.
Tap Pause to freeze a shot, then pin a trick. Tap a timeline shot to jump.
Compare the two pictures. Tap Plain view again to return to the ad.
Drag the ruler to the toy. Or focus it and use the arrow keys. Then tap Check alignment.
Tap Go, then tap Stop stopwatch when the racer reaches the one meter line.
Tap Try box only. Then tap Try with ramp and compare the jumps.
Tap Lights out. Watch the eyes before you mark the claim.
Tap Open the box. Compare its contents with the ad.
Tap two claim cards that support your message. Then tap Check my claim.
Your claims support that message. Tap Ratings to give your judgment.
Tick the rules the ad breaks, then tap Show the shots.
Add the four prices. Enter your total and tap Check total.
First do the test. Evidence comes before a stamp.
First pin a trick to this shot in The ad. Music can pin anywhere.
That stamp does not fit the evidence. Run this test again before choosing another stamp.
Zero is not lined up with the toy yet. Move the ruler into the dashed guide.
The toy measures 12 centimeters. Compare it with the ad, then choose a stamp below.
You stopped before the racer reached the line. Tap Go and try again.
The racer already crossed the line. Tap Go and try stopping closer to the crossing.
Watch both runs: 1.7 seconds in real life, about 0.57 in the ad. Then choose a stamp below.
Without a ramp, the toy rolls off the edge. Now tap Try with ramp.
With the extra ramp, it clears 10 centimeters. Compare that with the canyon, then choose a stamp below.
The eyes really glow in the dark. Compare that with the claim, then choose a stamp below.
One racer, one short track piece and stickers. The extras cost more. Choose a stamp below.
Eight racers are shown, each sold separately. That does not prove everyone has one. Choose a stamp below.
Test and stamp the claims in The lab before checking which rules this ad breaks.
Look at the picture again. Tap it, or focus it and press Enter, before trying another trick.
The camera is low here too, but that does not explain its speed. Look for a speed or sound technique.
Tap Pause, then tap a spot on the picture before choosing a trick. Enter on a trick card also pins it.
Choose a rating and add an evidence chip. Your rating itself has no right answer.
A new case. Tap Play to begin the ad again.
That total does not match the four prices. Add the dollars and cents, then check again.
The setup costs 65 dollars and 46 cents. That is 35 dollars and 47 cents more than the shouted price.
The camera is down low, looking up. That makes small things look big.
No low camera here. Look for the trick in this shot.
The toy fills the picture. With nothing for scale, the toy or its jump looks huge.
This shot shows the surroundings. A close-up is not its trick.
The film runs faster than the real toy. The background races past.
No sped-up film here: the background is not racing past.
The roar or boom adds power. The real plastic toy does not make that sound.
No added roar or boom in this shot. Try a different trick.
Cheering makes it feel like everyone wants one. Eight toys do not prove that everyone has one.
No cheering crowd in this shot. Listen, or read the sound caption.
Important facts flash past in tiny print. Track, ramp and batteries cost extra.
No tiny sales facts flash past in this shot. Find the price shot.
Music makes the toy feel exciting. That feeling is not evidence of what the toy can do.
